title: Bounded colimit relations present a presentable infinity category
statement:
Use the universes and coherent infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and presentability, regular cardinals, $\kappa$-small diagrams and $\kappa$-compact objects as defined in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Use the notation $P_R(A)$ for relative free cocompletion in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion]. Let $C$ be a presentable infinity category. There exist an infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$, a small infinity category $A$ admitting $\kappa$-small colimits, and a fully faithful functor $i:A\to C$ preserving those colimits, whose essential image is the subcategory of $\kappa$-compact objects of $C$. Every object of $C$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of objects in this image. Let $R$ be a small collection consisting of colimiting cocones in $A$ with $\kappa$-small bases, and containing a representative for every $\kappa$-small diagram in $A$, up to equivalence of diagrams and cocones. Then $i$ extends to a colimit-preserving equivalence $P_R(A)\simeq C$ over $A$. Equivalently, for every infinity category $Z$ admitting all small colimits, restriction along $i$ gives an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(C,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_R(A,Z).$$
Here the right side is the full coherent functor category on functors sending every member of $R$ to a colimiting cocone, or equivalently preserving $\kappa$-small colimits of $A$. The equivalence includes natural transformations and higher simplices and is natural in $Z$. The target $Z$ need not be presentable. All smallness and colimit assertions are relative to the original universe $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1, conditions (2)-(4) and proof, printed pp. 457-460; Example 5.3.6.8, p. 415 (completion under all small colimits of a small category with kappa-small colimit relations is its kappa-Ind completion); Proposition 5.3.5.10, p. 406; Proposition 5.5.1.9, p. 461. The universal property for arbitrary cocomplete targets is that of Proposition 5.3.6.2 after the equivalence of Example 5.3.6.8. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks Project tag states this quasicategorical theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-presentable-cardinal-enlargement] to $C$ and the empty set of arrows, and retain its regular cardinal $\kappa$. Then $C$ is $\kappa$-accessible and its full subcategory $C^\kappa$ of all $\kappa$-compact objects is essentially small. Choose a small infinity category $A$ and an equivalence $A\simeq C^\kappa$, and let $i:A\to C$ be the composite with the full inclusion. Every object of $C$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of objects in the image of $i$: this follows from the generating subcategory in the definition of $\kappa$-accessibility in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], whose objects are all in $C^\kappa$. A $\kappa$-small diagram in $A$ has a colimit in $C$ by presentability, and its apex is $\kappa$-compact by [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits]. Write $e:A\simeq C^\kappa$ for the chosen equivalence and $t$ for its coherent inverse. The cocone just constructed lies in the full subcategory $C^\kappa$; applying $t$ and the natural equivalence $1_A\simeq te$ gives a cocone on the original diagram $q:K\to A$, with apex $t(c)$. For $b\in A$, the map $\operatorname{Map}_A(t(c),b)\to\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_A(q(-),b)$ identifies, using $e$ and $et\simeq1$, with $\operatorname{Map}_C(c,i(b))\to\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_C(iq(-),i(b))$. This is an equivalence by the colimit property of $c$ in $C$. The mapping-space criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] therefore proves that this cocone is colimiting in $A$. Its image under $i$ is equivalent, by $et\simeq1$, to the original colimiting cocone with apex $c$, so $i$ preserves it.

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1, (1) implies (2)-(4), and proof; Proposition 5.4.2.2 and Corollary 5.3.4.15

proof.text: There is a small set of representative $\kappa$-small simplicial shapes: relabel their nondegenerate simplices by subsets of $\kappa$, and encode the simplicial operations by functions between the resulting small sets. Here the chosen $\kappa$ is uncountable, so adjoining all degeneracies still gives fewer than $\kappa$ simplices. For each representative $K$, maps $K\to A$ form a small set since $K,A$ are small. Choose a colimiting cocone in $A$ for each such map, using step 1; the collection $R_0$ of these choices is small. Colimiting cocones for a fixed diagram are unique up to coherent equivalence, since their mapping-space universal property represents the same cocone functor. Consequently $R_0$ gives the representatives required in the statement. In the remaining steps let $R$ be any small collection satisfying the statement, not just $R_0$. For any $f:A\to Z$, sending every member of $R$ to a colimiting cocone is equivalent to preserving every $\kappa$-small colimit: one direction uses that each member is such a colimit, and the other uses that every such cocone is equivalent to a representative and that equivalences identify its mapping-space universal property. This proves $\operatorname{Fun}_R(A,Z)=\operatorname{Fun}_{\kappa\text{-colim}}(A,Z)$ as full subcategories, including all transformations.

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1 and Example 5.3.6.8; small representative relations and invariance of the colimit universal property

proof.text: Put $\mathcal P(A)=\operatorname{Fun}(A^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ and $y(a)=\operatorname{Map}_A(-,a)$. The small mapping spaces and all small colimits of $\mathcal P(A)$ are supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion]; its colimits are computed objectwise by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Restrict the coherent Yoneda functor of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] along $i^{\mathrm{op}}$ to obtain $H:C\to\mathcal P(A)$ with $H(c)(a)=\operatorname{Map}_C(i(a),c)$; that node applies because $C$ is locally small and fits in the containing universe. Thus the values are coherently modeled by small spaces. Full faithfulness of $i$ gives a natural equivalence $Hi\simeq y$. For a small $\kappa$-filtered diagram $F:I\to C$, put $M_a=\operatorname{colim}_{t\in I}H(F(t))(a)$ in small spaces. By [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe], the fully faithful inclusion $\iota:\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$ carries this cocone to a colimit. Compactness of $i(a)$, in the convention of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], says that the cocone with apex $\iota H(\operatorname{colim}_I F)(a)$ is also colimiting in the larger space category. The canonical comparison $\iota M_a\to\iota H(\operatorname{colim}_I F)(a)$ is therefore an equivalence. Full faithfulness of $\iota$ reflects equivalences: lift the inverse through the mapping-space equivalence, and the two inverse equations hold after lifting because those mapping-space maps induce bijections on components. Thus $M_a\simeq H(\operatorname{colim}_I F)(a)$ in small spaces. The objectwise colimit criterion therefore says that $H$ preserves these colimits. If $c\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{t\in I}i(p(t))$ is a presentation from step 1, then $H(c)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{t\in I}y(p(t))$.

source.place: Propositions 5.3.5.10-5.3.5.11: restricted Yoneda and compact-generator comparison

proof.text:
The functor $H$ is fully faithful. Indeed, choose the presentation $c\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{t\in I}i(p(t))$ of step 3 and fix $d\in C$. Applying the mapping-space colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] first in $\mathcal P(A)$ and then in $C$, and using [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation] in the middle, gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(A)}(H(c),H(d))\simeq\lim_{t\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(A)}(y(p(t)),H(d))\simeq\lim_{t\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_C(i(p(t)),d)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_C(c,d).$$
The inverse of this composite is the map induced by $H$, because at each generator it is evaluation of a transformation on the identity and all maps arise from the presentation cocone. Thus these are natural mapping-space equivalences, not just bijections on homotopy classes.

Let $B\subseteq\mathcal P(A)$ be the full subcategory on presheaves taking every $\kappa$-small colimit in $A$ to a limit of spaces. The recognition lemma [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-ind-criterion] identifies its objects exactly with small $\kappa$-filtered colimits of representables. Step 3 shows that every $H(c)$ is in $B$. Conversely, if $X\simeq\operatorname{colim}_I yp$ is such a presheaf, form $c=\operatorname{colim}_I ip$ in $C$; step 3 gives $H(c)\simeq X$. Thus $B$ is precisely the full essential image of $H$. Together with step 4, [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] gives a coherent equivalence $H:C\simeq B$ and a quasi-inverse, with its natural equivalences. The generators $Hi\simeq y$ lie in this full subcategory.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4 and Proposition 5.3.5.11(2); Ind identification in Example 5.3.6.8

proof.text:
Use the explicit small-data model in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion]. It realizes $P_R(A)$ as the full subcategory of $\mathcal P(A)$ on presheaves $X$ local for every map $s_r:\operatorname{colim}_{K}yq\to y(a)$ arising from $r=(q:K\to A\,,q\to a)\in R$, and its generator is $j_R=Ly$, with $L$ the reflector. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] and [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation], precomposition with $s_r$ is exactly
$$X(a)\longrightarrow\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(q(-)).$$
Step 2 implies that all these maps are equivalences exactly when $X\in B$. Hence this explicit model of $P_R(A)$ is $B$. Each $y(a)$ is already in $B$ by step 5. For a full reflective inclusion $u:B\hookrightarrow\mathcal P(A)$, adjunction and full faithfulness give $\operatorname{Map}_B(Lu(b),b')\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(A)}(u(b),u(b'))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_B(b,b')$ naturally in $b'$, so the counit $Lu(b)\to b$ is an equivalence by the Yoneda criterion. This gives $j_R=Ly\simeq y$ naturally. Compose the equivalence $P_R(A)=B\simeq C$ of step 5 to obtain $E$; then $Ej_R\simeq i$. An equivalence preserves every existing small colimit: testing a cocone against an arbitrary target object, a quasi-inverse identifies its mapping-space colimit criterion on both sides. Therefore $E$ is the required colimit-preserving equivalence, entirely in the original small-colimit universe.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.2 and Example 5.3.6.8: local-presheaf model and identification over A

proof.text: For an arbitrary infinity category $Z$ admitting all original-universe small colimits, precomposition with $E:P_R(A)\simeq C$ gives an equivalence of full coherent functor categories $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(C,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(P_R(A),Z)$. An inverse is precomposition with its quasi-inverse; both preserve the defining class of functors by the preceding colimit argument. Compose this with the unary restriction equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion] to obtain $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(C,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_R(A,Z)$. Since $Ej_R\simeq i$, the composite is restriction along $i$. The cited restriction equivalence includes transformations and all higher simplices and is natural in $Z$; composition with $E$ and its coherent inverse retains these properties. Here naturality is with respect to colimit-preserving functors between cocomplete targets. The cited node allows arbitrary cocomplete $Z$, so no presentability assumption on $Z$ or enlargement of the class of permitted small diagrams has been used.
